categories.description: Fully managed, vendor-hosted LLMs exposed as simple APIs. You send prompts; the provider handles hosting, scaling, safety features, and updates.
Hyperscaler and data-cloud platforms that host foundation models with governance, tuning, evals, monitoring, RAG, and cloud integrations.
Specialized providers focused on high-performance model serving, fine-tuning, batch jobs, and dedicated or serverless endpoints.
Abstraction layers for routing, fallback, caching, observability, cost controls, guardrails, and policy across many model providers.
Raw GPU compute, GPU clusters, or serverless GPU pods you control to run your own inference stack.
Turnkey software/hardware stacks to run LLMs in private data centers, including regulated and air-gapped environments.
Self-hostable runtimes/servers for deploying LLMs anywhere, including cloud, on-prem, and private clusters.
Desktop apps/CLIs that download and run models on a laptop, workstation, or local server.
SDKs/runtimes to run compact or optimized models directly on phones, PCs with NPUs, or embedded/edge devices.

options.name: OpenAI API
options.notes: Managed GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol, plus image, voice, realtime, and embeddings APIs. The Agents API entered public beta on September 10 (hosted-browser computer use added September 29); Ultrafast mode now covers GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and a beta Decisions API launched October 6.

options.name: Claude API
options.notes: Managed Claude 5.5 models: Opus 5.5 (September 22, $4/$20 per million tokens, fast mode in research preview), Sonnet 5.5 (September 28), and Haiku 5.5 (October 7, 1M-token context), alongside Fable 5.1. Managed Agents gained auto permission policies and beta dynamic multi-agent workflows; Sonnet 4.5 retires from the API on November 30.

options.name: Gemini API
options.notes: Managed Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 3.8 Live audio-to-audio models (GA September 15), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS with voice design and replication (GA September 22), and Nano Banana 2.1 image generation (GA October 6). Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.5 Flash were deprecated on October 8 and are routed to newer Flash models.

options.name: Azure OpenAI Service
options.notes: OpenAI models on Azure with enterprise identity, networking, and governance controls. GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna are available in Microsoft Foundry as of September 22 for production agents and high-volume workloads; access depends on deployment availability and quota.

options.name: Cohere API
options.notes: Managed Command, Embed, Rerank, and document-intelligence APIs, with Model Vault for isolated inference. Parse launched August 27 at $1.50 per 1,000 pages, with Model Vault and private-infrastructure deployment options.

options.name: Mistral La Plateforme (API)
options.notes: Managed Mistral language, coding, OCR, speech, and moderation models with agent and retrieval tools, plus hosted partner models such as Z.ai GLM 5.3 (GA September 28). Mistral Large 4, an open-weight multimodal MoE model with a 1M-token context window, entered public preview on October 6; OCR 4.0 retired in favour of OCR 4.1.

options.name: AI21 Studio / AI21 API
options.notes: Jamba/J2 models, text & embeddings.

options.name: Aleph Alpha API
options.notes: Luminous/Alpha family with multimodal & explainability.

options.name: Grok API
options.notes: Managed Grok reasoning, coding, voice, and image-generation models through compatible APIs. Grok 4.7 launched in September with a 500K-token context window and tiered pricing, and Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0 became the default speech-to-text model after 1.0 reached end of life on October 2.

options.name: DeepSeek API
options.notes: Managed DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4.1 Flash with Responses-compatible access and 1M-token context. V4.1 Flash, the first model of a new architecture family with native visual understanding, launched September 10 with lower API prices and replaced V4 Flash and V4 Flash Vision.

options.name: Meta Model API
options.notes: API access to Meta's Muse models, including Muse Spark 1.3 with max reasoning from September 2. Muse Voice Transcribe launched September 1 for streaming speech recognition, speaker diarization, and endpointing.

options.name: QwenCloud
options.notes: Managed Qwen and partner-model APIs, including Qwen3.8 Max and Flash, realtime omni, speech, translation, image, and video models. September–October additions include Qwen3.8 Omni Flash Realtime, a decision-model preview for classification and scoring, Qwen-Image 2.1 Pro, and hosted DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

options.name: Amazon Bedrock
options.notes: Managed multi-provider model platform with regional endpoints and enterprise controls. OpenAI GPT-6 Astra became generally available on September 8, and Claude Opus 5.5 arrived September 22 with US, EU, AU, JP, and global cross-Region inference profiles.

options.name: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
options.notes: Deploy 400+ open-weights FMs incl. DeepSeek, Llama, Mistral.

options.name: Vertex AI (Generative AI)
options.notes: Google Cloud managed Gemini and partner-model access with grounding, tuning, evaluation, and model lifecycle controls. Current access includes Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude Fable 5.1; model, feature, and regional availability vary.

options.name: Microsoft Foundry - Model Catalog
options.notes: Managed model catalog spanning OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft MAI, and other providers. September 22 additions include GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 for long-running coding and knowledge work; model access and quotas vary by deployment.

options.name: IBM watsonx.ai
options.notes: Granite + third-party/open models; Model Gateway.

options.name: Snowflake Cortex
options.notes: Built-in LLM functions and model access inside Snowflake.

options.name: Databricks Mosaic AI Model Serving
options.notes: Managed serving for custom, open-weight, and partner models through Foundation Model APIs and Unity Gateway. Unity Gateway APIs and developer tools became GA on September 16, with a ug CLI connecting coding agents; new models include GPT-6 Sol/Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, Grok 4.7, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.

options.name: Oracle OCI Generative AI
options.notes: Managed generative AI (models & tuning).

options.name: Hugging Face Inference Endpoints
options.notes: Hosted endpoints with autoscaling & TGI/vLLM engines.

options.name: Together AI
options.notes: High-throughput open-model inference and fine-tuning platform with serverless and dedicated endpoints. Together Link (October 5) connects coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex to open models like GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 with automatic routing, and its dedicated NVIDIA B300 cluster on IBM Cloud is now offered for enterprise inference.

options.name: Fireworks AI
options.notes: Fast inference, fine-tuning, and RL for open models, also offered inside the Microsoft Foundry catalog. Ember-1, a Kimi K3-based model using about 40% fewer reasoning tokens, entered serverless research preview on September 23, and GLOBAL deployments now pool GPU capacity across regions behind a single endpoint.

options.name: Replicate
options.notes: Run models as APIs; deploy your own containers.

options.name: Baseten
options.notes: Production LLM inference; dedicated deployments.

options.name: Modal
options.notes: Bring-your-code serverless GPU compute for inference.

options.name: GroqCloud
options.notes: Ultra-low-latency inference for supported open models on Groq LPUs; joined the NVIDIA Cloud Partner program to add NVIDIA accelerated capacity alongside LPUs.

options.name: Cerebras Inference
options.notes: High-throughput LLM inference on Cerebras wafer-scale hardware with OpenAI-compatible chat completions and dedicated endpoints; also powers OpenAI's Ultrafast tier for GPT-5.6 Sol (up to 750 tokens/s).

options.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
options.notes: Serverless GPU inference on Cloudflare's global network, unified with AI Gateway for Workers AI and third-party models. Cloudflare launched Clef and Clef-flash, its first open-source (Apache 2.0) decision models returning typed probabilities, on October 1, followed by multimodal Clef-omni on October 9.

options.name: Nebius AI Studio
options.notes: Managed open-source model inference for text, embeddings, image, guardrails, and vision workloads with configurable GPU-backed endpoint flavors.

options.name: OpenRouter
options.notes: Meta-API routing across hundreds of models and providers with evaluation, spend controls, and observability. September–October additions include US in-region routing (alongside EU), a half-price Batch API across 70+ models, an API-key Security Center, and ElevenLabs speech models.

options.name: Portkey
options.notes: Model catalog, routing, guardrails, observability.

options.name: Helicone Gateway
options.notes: Routing, caching, telemetry for LLM APIs.

options.name: CoreWeave
options.notes: GPU VMs & inference stacks for self-hosting.

options.name: Lambda Cloud
options.notes: On-demand GPUs & clusters for training/inference.

options.name: Crusoe Cloud
options.notes: Sustainable GPU cloud for AI workloads.

options.name: RunPod
options.notes: Pods & serverless GPUs; templates for TGI/vLLM/SGLang.

options.name: Vast.ai
options.notes: Spot rental GPUs; TGI serverless templates.

options.name: VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA
options.notes: NVIDIA NIM microservices, Model Store, secure on-prem AI.

options.name: Red Hat OpenShift AI
options.notes: Lifecycle mgmt & serving for predictive/gen-AI at scale.

options.name: HPE Private Cloud AI
options.notes: Turnkey AI factory systems with NVIDIA GPUs.

options.name: Dell AI Factory / Platforms
options.notes: Validated designs & turnkey ‘AI factory’ systems.

options.name: NVIDIA NIM
options.notes: Inference microservices for LLMs (NGC, Triton, TensorRT-LLM).

options.name: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
options.notes: Multi-framework inference server; LLM backends incl. TensorRT-LLM.

options.name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
options.notes: High-performance LLM runtime and kernels for NVIDIA GPUs, also used as a Triton backend. The v1.3.0 release candidates (rc26–rc29, September) add DeepSeek-V4 Hopper and Rubin kernel support, Anthropic-compatible Messages APIs in trtllm-serve, and KV-cache manager V2 by default.

options.name: KServe
options.notes: CRDs for serving predictive & generative models; LLM features.

options.name: Seldon Core
options.notes: K8s-native model serving & monitoring.

options.name: Ray Serve (LLM APIs)
options.notes: Distributed LLM serving with OpenAI-compatible APIs.

options.name: BentoML (LLM serving)
options.notes: Packaging & scaling LLM services; speculative decoding optimizations.

options.name: vLLM
options.notes: High-throughput open-source model serving with paged KV cache and a Rust frontend. v0.29–v0.31 (September 9 – October 5) made Model Runner V2 the default, added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with NVFP4 KV cache, weight-cache preloading for fast restarts, and prefill context parallelism.

options.name: Text Generation Inference (TGI)
options.notes: Hugging Face inference server in maintenance mode since December 2025. Existing deployments remain supported, but Hugging Face recommends vLLM or SGLang for new production workloads.

options.name: SGLang
options.notes: Open-source serving engine for language, vision-language, and diffusion models. v0.5.21 (October 2) lets prefill/decode instances switch roles without restart, moves the prefix cache to a Rust core, and adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash plus Decisions and Score APIs.

options.name: LMDeploy (TurboMind/PyTorch engines)
options.notes: Inference/serving toolkit; supports popular OSS models.

options.name: llama.cpp
options.notes: CPU/GPU-portable LLM inference in C/C++; quantization support.

options.name: Ollama
options.notes: Local model runner and cloud model service with compatible APIs and integrations for coding tools. v0.35 (September 28) added decision models such as Clef, Nimble, and Tev1 that return choices and probabilities, and v0.40 (September 25) runs supported architectures on the MLX engine by default on Apple Silicon.

options.name: LM Studio
options.notes: Desktop runtime for local models, with Bionic combining local and US-hosted open models for agent tasks. September updates added session references and introspection across compactions and the Splash engine for fast local Qwen3.8 on Apple Silicon.

options.name: GPT4All (Desktop)
options.notes: Fully local chatbot app; optional local API server.

options.name: Koboldcpp
options.notes: Lightweight UI/server for local LLMs; roleplay/story use cases.

options.name: MLC LLM
options.notes: WebGPU & native runtimes for local OSS models.

options.name: Apple MLX / mlx-lm
options.notes: Apple-optimized local LLM library on MLX.

options.name: Intel OpenVINO GenAI
options.notes: Optimized CPU/iGPU inference for LLMs with quantization.

options.name: ONNX Runtime GenAI
options.notes: Run SLMs/LLMs on CPU/GPU/NPU; Windows ML & DirectML support.

options.name: NVIDIA Jetson (Generative AI/NIM on Jetson)
options.notes: Embedded LLM/VLM deployment on Jetson platforms.

options.name: Qualcomm AI Hub (on-device)
options.notes: On-device LLM workflows for Snapdragon platforms.

options.name: Argonne ALCF Inference Endpoints
options.notes: API access to OSS models on HPC hardware.

options.name: Z.ai API
options.notes: Managed GLM reasoning, coding, and multimodal APIs. GLM-5.3-Flash launched August 26 with 1M-token context and Coding Plan access; published weights also support independent self-hosting.

options.name: Tencent Cloud TokenHub
options.notes: Tencent Cloud API access to Hy models, including Hy3 and the open-weight Hy4 Preview released August 28. Hy4 Preview supports coding, office work, and research with a context window exceeding 1M tokens.
